cards.explanation: The answer is rest. Jesus says, “Come with Me privately to a solitary place, and let us rest for a while.” Many people were coming and going, and the apostles did not even have time to eat. I think that sounds like a week where a nap feels like a vacation. Rest was the invitation, friends.

The answer is that they run there on foot and get there first. They saw the boat leave and recognized who was in it. Then they ran together on foot from all the towns and arrived before Jesus and the apostles (Mark 6:33). Think about that: people on foot beat a boat. I can't even beat my own oven timer to the oven.

The answer is False. Jesus does not send the crowd away. He stepped ashore, saw the large crowd, and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. So instead of leaving, He began to teach them many things.

The answer is that He begins to teach them many things. Mark says Jesus saw a large crowd and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. Then He began to teach them many things. Notice the order, friends: compassion first, then teaching. I think a shepherd leads, and Jesus starts leading with His words.

The answer is True. The disciples say, “Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat.” They point out that it's a desolate place and the hour is already late. Jesus answers with something they didn't see coming.

The answer is far too little to go around. Jesus tells them to go and see how many loaves they have. After checking, they say, “Five—and two fish.” Remember, they'd just asked whether to spend two hundred denarii to give all of them bread to eat. Next to that crowd, five loaves and two fish is far too little to go around.

The answer is to sit down in groups on the green grass. Jesus directs them to have the people sit in groups on the green grass, and they sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties. He gives that direction with only five loaves and two fish to work with. I think there's something calm about grass and orderly groups, friends.
The answer is True. Taking the five loaves and the two fish, Jesus looked up to heaven and spoke a blessing. Then He broke the loaves. The blessing comes first, friends.

The answer is True. After breaking the loaves, Jesus gave them to His disciples to set before the people. He also divided the two fish among them all. So the disciples were the ones putting the food in front of the crowd.
The word is satisfied. They all ate and were satisfied. That means a whole crowd, not just the front row. And that was from five loaves and two fish.

The answer is twelve basketfuls. The disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces of bread and fish. That came after everyone ate and was satisfied, and it all started with five loaves and two fish. Twelve baskets, friends. My leftovers after a long baking day fit in a single cookie tin.
